ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that point $M$ is the midpoint of line segment $AB$, point $N$ is on line segment $MB$, $AM=\frac{5}{3}MN$, if $MN=3\,cm$, find the lengths of line segments $AB$ and $NB$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AM= \frac{5}{3}MN$, and $MN=3\,\text{cm}$\\
$\therefore AM=5\,\text{cm}$\\
Furthermore, since point $M$ is the midpoint of line segment $AB$\\
$\therefore AM=BM= \frac{1}{2}AB$,\\
$\therefore AB=\boxed{10\,\text{cm}}$\\
Also, since $NB=AB-AM-MN$,\\
$\therefore NB=\boxed{2\,\text{cm}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I looked at the attached figure; in the figure there is a horizontal line segment, and the order of the points from left to right is A, M, N, B. Therefore N is between M and B, and the whole line segment AB is divided into three parts: AM, MN, and NB. Reasoning: It is known that MN = 3 cm, and AM = 5/3 × MN, so AM = 5/3 × 3 = 5 cm. Also because M is the midpoint of AB, AM = MB = 5 cm, therefore AB = AM + MB = 5 + 5 = 10 cm. Since N is on line segment MB, NB = MB - MN = 5 - 3 = 2 cm.
